priorStories.headline: Asian stocks plunge in AI-share sell-off
priorStories.body:
A sell-off in artificial-intelligence-related shares sent South Korea’s Kospi down 7.6% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 down 4.9%.

U.S. stocks recovered by the close. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 556 points, while the Nasdaq Composite finished about 20 points higher.

priorStories.headline: Four killed at Oregon elementary school
priorStories.body:
A 16-year-old shot through locked doors and entered Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, authorities said. Three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a teacher were killed. A 7-year-old child and another teacher were hospitalized in critical condition.

Authorities said a person at the scene followed the attacker inside and shot him. Police found the attacker dead minutes after the first emergency call.

priorStories.headline: Istanbul floods kill three, force evacuations
priorStories.body:
Heavy rain flooded homes, roads and underpasses across Istanbul, leaving three people dead and four missing as of Thursday. Turkey’s interior minister said more than 2,700 stranded people were evacuated.

Schools remained closed. Officials said some districts received their heaviest rainfall since 1985.

priorStories.headline: Peshawar school collapse kills 35
priorStories.body:
A private school’s roof collapsed during classes in Peshawar, killing 34 children and a teacher, according to an updated Associated Press account. More than 50 people were injured as rescue crews searched the rubble.

An earlier Reuters report carried a lower death toll.

priorStories.headline: U.S. wholesale prices jump 1.3%
priorStories.body:
The producer price index for final demand rose a seasonally adjusted 1.3% in September, the largest monthly increase since March 2022. Wholesale prices were 6.3% higher than a year earlier.

Goods prices increased 2.6%, while services prices rose 0.8%. Energy and transportation costs contributed to the acceleration.

candidates.summary: Saudi organizers said preparations for the 2027 Asian Cup remain on schedule despite escalating regional conflict and recent Houthi attacks inside Saudi Arabia. The Asian Football Confederation has said it could postpone the tournament if security conditions require it, with a decision possible by the end of November.
candidates.title: Saudi organizers say Asian Cup remains on schedule

candidates.summary: Russian attacks hit nine Ukrainian regions overnight, wounding at least 15 people and cutting electricity to hundreds of thousands of households, Ukrainian officials said. Separately, Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces intercepted 644 Ukrainian drones; airport restrictions delayed more than 200 flights from four Moscow airports and delayed or canceled 46 flights in St. Petersburg.
candidates.title: Overnight attacks disrupt power and flights in Ukraine and Russia

candidates.summary: Hot, windy conditions fueled several Southern California brush fires Friday. A Malibu fire prompted evacuation orders and warnings across part of the Santa Monica Mountains, while the 147-acre Bryson Fire was 17% contained Friday morning. More than 175,000 California electricity customers lacked power, including customers affected by preventive utility shutoffs during elevated fire danger.
candidates.title: Southern California fires prompt evacuations amid high winds

candidates.summary: Katie Zacharia was leaving her role as White House press secretary after five days on the job, the Associated Press reported, citing a person familiar with the personnel decision. Axios, citing two senior administration officials, reported that Zacharia had been ousted.
candidates.title: Katie Zacharia leaves White House press secretary role

candidates.summary: U.S. stocks closed lower Friday as technology shares extended their sell-off. The S&P 500 fell 1.1%, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.1% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.3%. The Nasdaq ended the week down 4.5%, its worst weekly performance since June.
candidates.title: U.S. stocks fall as technology sell-off continues

The Associated Press reported that at least six homes burned, about 16,000 residents were ordered to evacuate and two firefighters were hospitalized with heat-related injuries.
candidates.title: Norte Fire burns homes and forces evacuations in Orange County

candidates.summary: The reported death toll from flooding in Istanbul rose Friday. The Associated Press reported four deaths after a missing man's body was recovered in the Sariyer district. Turkish news outlet Bianet reported five deaths, also counting a construction worker who died after falling into a flooded well, and said searches continued for at least five missing people.
candidates.title: Reported Istanbul flood death toll rises to five
